title: Impact of Wilderness Designation on Deforestation

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy  
Causal method: Sharp Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD)

Why: Wilderness status is assigned mechanically when elevation crosses a legislated cutoff. Observations infinitesimally above and below that elevation are plausibly identical in every respect except for being inside vs. outside the wilderness boundary, providing quasi-random variation.

Key identifying assumptions  
• Continuity: In the absence of the policy, the conditional expectation of deforestation would be continuous in elevation at the cutoff.  
• No precise manipulation: Land owners cannot perfectly sort parcels around the exact elevation that triggers wilderness designation.

If these hold, the jump in the outcome at the cutoff is the causal effect of wilderness designation on deforestation.

---

## 2. R Code
```r
#########################################################################
# Impact of Wilderness Designation on Deforestation – Sharp RDD
# File: experiments/exp_b/data/s93_data.csv
#########################################################################

# 1. Load packages ------------------------------------------------------
need <- c("data.table","rdrobust","ggplot2")
new  <- need[!need %in% installed.packages()[,"Package"]]
if(length(new)) install.packages(new, repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
lapply(need, library, character.only = TRUE)

# 2. Import data --------------------------------------------------------
path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s93_data.csv"
df   <- fread(path)

# 3. Locate the cutoff empirically -------------------------------------
#   The assignment rule is deterministic but the exact threshold is not given.
#   We recover it as the midpoint between the highest untreated and lowest treated
#   elevation values inside the 'near_cutoff' window provided by the researcher.
lo  <- max(df[treated==0 & near_cutoff==1, running_var])
hi  <- min(df[treated==1 & near_cutoff==1, running_var])
cut <- (lo + hi)/2
cat(sprintf("Elevation cutoff inferred at: %.4f\n\n", cut))

# 4. Main RDD estimate (local‐linear, MSE-optimal bandwidth) ------------
main <- rdrobust(y = df$y, x = df$running_var, c = cut)
print(main)

# 5. Robustness checks --------------------------------------------------
## (a) Alternative bandwidths: half & double the MSE-optimal
bws <- c(main$bws[1]/2, main$bws[1]*2)
alt1 <- rdrobust(y = df$y, x = df$running_var, c = cut, h = bws[1])
alt2 <- rdrobust(y = df$y, x = df$running_var, c = cut, h = bws[2])

## (b) Higher-order polynomial (quadratic)
quad <- rdrobust(y = df$y, x = df$running_var, c = cut, p = 2)

# 6. Display key numbers ------------------------------------------------
cat("\n================  Summary of Estimates  ================\n")
out <- rbind(
  c("Main (LL, MSE-opt h)" , main$coef[1],  main$se[1]),
  c("Half-bandwidth"       , alt1$coef[1],  alt1$se[1]),
  c("Double-bandwidth"     , alt2$coef[1],  alt2$se[1]),
  c("Quadratic poly"       , quad$coef[1],  quad$se[1])
)
colnames(out) <- c("Specification","ATE","SE")
print(out, row.names = FALSE)

# 7. Simple RD plot -----------------------------------------------------
ggplot(df, aes(x = running_var, y = y)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = cut, colour = "red", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_smooth(data = df[running_var <  cut], method = "lm", se = FALSE, colour = "blue") +
  geom_smooth(data = df[running_var >= cut], method = "lm", se = FALSE, colour = "darkgreen") +
  labs(title = "RDD Plot – Deforestation vs. Elevation",
       x = "Elevation (running variable)",
       y = "Deforestation rate") +
  theme_minimal()
```

---

## 3. Expected Findings  
Economic intuition suggests that wilderness designation restricts logging and land clearing, so parcels just inside the boundary should exhibit lower deforestation. Hence:

• Sign: Negative jump at the cutoff (treated minus control < 0).  
• Magnitude: With deforestation rates expressed as fractions, a 10–25 percentage-point reduction (≈ −0.10 to −0.25) is plausible near the threshold.

Robustness checks (bandwidth and polynomial order) should leave the sign unchanged and keep the effect within the same ballpark, reinforcing the credibility of the causal claim.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Compare deforestation rates just above and below the elevation cutoff.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Wilderness designation is associated with a moderate increase in deforestation rates.
